questions_and_answers.question: All else held constant, interest rate risk will increase when the time to maturity: a.) decreases or the coupon rate increases. b.) decreases or the coupon rate decreases. c.) increases or the coupon rate increases. d.) increases or the coupon rate decreases. e.) decreases and the coupon rate equals zero.
questions_and_answers.answer: The correct answer is D- Increases or the coupon rate decreases. This is because interest rate risk affects bond value as it directly affects fixed income securities value. There is an inverse relationship between prices of bond and interest rates hence, when the interest rate rises the prices of the bond will fall and vice versa. The interest rate of a bond is the coupon rate or in other words its each year`s payment to bondholders. A bonds maturity is the future specific date that its face value will be repaid to the investor. There will be increase in interest rate risk when maturity period is longer. There will be increase in interest rate risk when coupon rate decreases.

related_questions.question: What is the interest rate risk?

text_blocks.snippet: Interest rate risk is the potential for investment losses due to changes in interest rates. It primarily affects fixed-income investments like bonds, where rising interest rates can decrease bond values. This is because new bonds will likely be issued with higher yields, making older, lower-yielding bonds less attractive.

list.title: Impact on Bond Prices:
list.snippet: When interest rates rise, the market value of existing bonds generally falls. This is because new bonds will be issued with higher interest rates, making older bonds with lower rates less desirable.

list.title: Inverse Relationship:
list.snippet: There's an inverse relationship between interest rates and bond prices. When interest rates go up, bond prices go down, and vice versa, according to the Corporate Finance Institute.

list.title: Fixed-Income Securities:
list.snippet: Interest rate risk is particularly relevant for fixed-income securities like bonds because their value is directly tied to prevailing interest rates.

list.title: Example:
list.snippet: If you own a bond with a fixed interest rate of 3%, and new bonds are issued with a 4% rate, your 3% bond will likely decrease in value because investors will prefer the higher-yielding option.

list.title: Bank's Perspective:
list.snippet: For banks, interest rate risk can arise from mismatches between the interest rates they earn on loans and the interest rates they pay on deposits, according to the FDIC. If interest rates rise, banks may have to pay more for deposits than they earn on their loans, potentially impacting their profitability.

text_blocks.snippet: Interest rate risk decreases as the time to maturity decreases and increases as the coupon rate decreases.

list.title: Time to Maturity:
list.snippet: Shorter-term bonds are less susceptible to interest rate fluctuations because the investor has less time to be exposed to potential changes in the market. When the time to maturity is short, the bond's price is less affected by interest rate changes compared to longer-term bonds.

list.title: Coupon Rate:
list.snippet: Lower coupon rates make a bond more sensitive to interest rate changes. This is because a smaller portion of the bond's value comes from the periodic coupon payments, and a larger portion comes from the final principal repayment. When interest rates rise, the present value of that principal repayment becomes more discounted, leading to a larger price decrease for bonds with lower coupon rates.
